children.text: What children learn in our preschool

Our preschool follows a play-based curriculum built on Experience Early Learning. Each week has a theme, and children explore it through stories, songs, art, building, pretend play and simple science. A developmental continuum helps us see what each child can do and what to work on next, so your child is never pushed too fast or held back.

Every day starts with circle time: we go over the calendar and the weather, practice letters and numbers, and talk about the day ahead. A picture schedule on the classroom wall helps younger children know what comes next, which makes the day calmer for everyone.
We welcome children from 2½ years old. Our youngest preschoolers work on talking, sharing, listening and taking turns, and many are still
, which we support together with you. Older children move on to
: writing their name, counting, following two-step directions and getting ready for a full school day.

image.alt: Uriah Child Care building on W Chestnut Ave in Vineland, NJ, with Now Enrolling flags

intro: Uriah Child Care welcomes Bridgeton, NJ families at our licensed center at 30 W Chestnut Ave in Vineland, about a 25-minute drive. We are open Monday to Sunday, 6 am to 11 pm, with toddler care, preschool and before and after school care for ages 2.5 and up. We accept NJ childcare subsidy (CCAP).
excerpt: Licensed care for Bridgeton families at our Vineland center, about 25 minutes away, open 7 days.

children.text: Many Bridgeton parents work in Vineland, at the hospital, in warehouses and food plants or in stores along Delsea Drive. Our center at 30 W Chestnut Ave is about a 25-minute drive from Bridgeton, so you can drop off on the way to work.
Monday to Sunday, 6 am to 11 pm
first, second and third shift care

faqs.question: How far is your center from Bridgeton?
faqs.answer: Our center is at 30 W Chestnut Ave in Vineland, about a 25-minute drive from Bridgeton.

faqs.question: Can I use CCAP if I live in Bridgeton?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bridgeton and Vineland are both in Cumberland County, and we accept NJ childcare subsidy (CCAP) for families who qualify.
